content: Dr. Victor Ling is a distinguished Canadian medical researcher who has received numerous accolades for his contributions to the field of medicine. His primary area of research is drug resistance in cancer, and he is most renowned for his groundbreaking discovery of P-glycoprotein, a key protein responsible for multidrug resistance in cancer cells. Dr. Ling was born in China and immigrated to Canada during his childhood. He completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Toronto in 1966 and earned his PhD from the University of British Columbia in 1969. In 2006, he was honored with an honorary doctorate from Trinity Western University. Following his doctoral studies, he pursued post-doctoral training under the mentorship of Nobel laureate Dr. Fred Sanger at Cambridge University. Currently, Dr. Ling holds the position of Assistant Dean of the Faculty of Medicine at the University of British Columbia. He also serves as Vice-President of Discovery at the BC Cancer Agency, located in Vancouver, British Columbia. Dr. Ling has been the recipient of several prestigious awards throughout his career. In 1990, he was awarded the Gairdner Award by the Gairdner Foundation for his exceptional contributions to medical science. In 1991, he received both the Charles F. Kettering Prize and the Steiner Award, the latter being the highest honor in cancer research. In 1994, he was further recognized with the Robert L. Noble Prize.
